title: Equal-capacity time-varying gravitational strength search on fresh high-redshift baryonic galaxy kinematics
hypothesis: One universal or explicitly local-clock evolution law for effective gravitational strength predicts fresh baryonic circular velocities across cosmic epoch better than a calibrated baryonic relation and a flexible ordinary evolution model while satisfying independent present-day and historical bounds.

discovery_policy.universal_gravity_track: Require one unchanged gravitational-strength evolution cell to improve fresh high-redshift baryonic kinematics, broad redshift and mass halves, ordinary nuisance models, selection-aware nulls, and every applicable external gravity bound.
discovery_policy.phenomenon_publication_track: Retain a reproducible redshift, transition, maturity, or oscillatory relation that beats ordinary held-out controls on its actual domain even if it cannot explain all missing gravity or pass as a universal theory.

theory.response_rule: At fixed baryonic calibration, circular speed receives delta_log10_V=0.5*log10(mu_G), where mu_G=G_eff/G0 is generated by one frozen cosmic or local-clock evolution cell.
theory.normalization: Every candidate has mu_G=1 at z=0 for a mature local system; cosmic families are exactly normalized at z=0 for all systems.
theory.local_clock_proxy: The local-settling niche uses the target-blind converted-baryon fraction Mstar/Mbar and cosmic age fraction only as a maturity clock; it is one equal-capacity peer and is not asserted to be causal age.

external_bounds.label: Alvey et al. improved BBN constraint
Ooba et al. Planck plus BAO scalar-tensor constraint
Williams, Turyshev, and Boggs lunar laser ranging
Bussieres, Caldarola, and Nesseris updated binary-pulsar analysis
external_bounds.scope: J1713+0747 dotG/G=(0.32+/-0.31)e-12 per year at 95 percent

prior_equivalence: The smooth-power niche is a known scalar-tensor or phenomenological varying-G control and is never labeled novel.
A bounded temporal transition is a known-family extension; a fit is not historical novelty.
The local-settling niche is potentially a new synthesis only if its maturity dependence varies on held-out support and is not reducible to a gas-fraction regression.
Oscillatory gravitational strength has scalar-field precedents; only the exact synthesis may be behaviorally distinct, and historical novelty requires a separate audit.
Algebraic non-equivalence is not evidence of historical novelty.
claim_limits: A baryonic Tully-Fisher residual is not a direct measurement of G and is strongly confounded by size, gas calibration, pressure support, selection, and evolving galaxy structure.
The recombination cutoff used here is deliberately conservative and broader than the cited model-specific Planck plus BAO result; passing it is not a full CMB likelihood.
The BBN and local derivative bounds are frozen falsification gates, not fitted response targets.
No positive result is a paper claim until the identical formula survives an unchanged fresh source.

sources.catalog_title: KMOS3D Tully-Fisher sample, Ubler et al. 2017

observable_lineage.baryons: Published SED stellar mass plus gas estimate in the KMOS3D baryonic mass, frozen before response access.
observable_lineage.epoch: Spectroscopic galaxy redshift, frozen before response access.
observable_lineage.maturity_proxy: Mstar/Mbar computed only from frozen baryonic predictors.
observable_lineage.response: Maximum pressure-support-corrected modeled circular velocity, queried by individual exploration sequence only after sample and candidate freeze.

sample.rule: After predictor-only validity checks, rank redshift and divide all 135 rows into five equal-rank strata. Seal five HMAC-ranked identities per stratum and assign the remaining identities to five stratum-balanced folds before querying any Vcirc.

candidate_generator.algorithm: numpy.random.Generator(PCG64) with four exactly balanced mechanism niches before response-independent historical and local filters

evaluation.baseline_calibrated_baryonic: training-only affine logVcirc versus logMbar relation
evaluation.baseline_flexible_nuisance: fixed ridge regression on logMbar, stellar fraction, sigma0, redshift, redshift squared, and predeclared interactions
